claims.text: Class-balanced demonstration sampling yields higher AUPR and AUROC scores for misclassification detection compared to random demonstration sampling across NLU benchmark datasets.
Epistemic uncertainty achieves an AUROC of 0.941 for out-of-domain demonstration detection on the EMOTION dataset using LLaMA-2-13B.
Epistemic uncertainty achieves an AUROC of 0.658 for semantic out-of-distribution detection on the EMOTION dataset using LLaMA-2-7B.
Predictive uncertainty in in-context learning can be decomposed into aleatoric uncertainty from demonstration variation and epistemic uncertainty from model parameters using mutual information.

evidence.description: In Table 1, LLaMA-7B-CLASS achieves higher AUPR and ROC scores than LLaMA-7B-RANDOM across datasets such as EMOTION (0.745 vs 0.688 ROC for EU) and SST-2 (0.701 vs 0.683 ROC for EU).
Table 3 shows EU reaching 0.941 ROC on out-of-domain demonstration detection using LLaMA-2-13B on the EMOTION dataset, outperforming Semantic Uncertainty (0.712) and Aleatoric Uncertainty (0.607).
Table 4 reports an AUROC of 0.658 for EU on semantic out-of-distribution detection using LLaMA-2-7B on the EMOTION dataset compared to 0.532 for Semantic Uncertainty.
Equations (2) and (3) derive aleatoric uncertainty via mutual information between output and latent concept, separating it from expected conditional entropy representing epistemic uncertainty.

methodologies.name: Entropy-based Uncertainty Decomposition
methodologies.description: Decomposes predictive uncertainty into epistemic and aleatoric components by calculating differential entropy and mutual information over normalized answer token probabilities obtained via beam search across sampled demonstration sets.

methodologies.name: Variance-based Uncertainty Decomposition
methodologies.description: Decomposes predictive uncertainty using the law of total variance applied to expected output values across model configurations and demonstration sets without needing access to token probabilities.

limitations.text: Existing uncertainty quantification works for LLMs overlook the reliance on provided in-context demonstrations and fail to provide insights into the underlying causes of uncertainty.
The proposed uncertainty estimation algorithm has limited usage in free-form generation tasks because identifying semantically important tokens in generated sequence parts is non-trivial.
The evaluation and framework are primarily restricted to deterministic natural language understanding tasks such as multiple-choice QA, text classification, and linguistic acceptability.

future_work.text: Extend the uncertainty decomposition method to other data modalities and complex text generation tasks.
